newsitem.title: JAPAN: Asian copper higher, traders focus on Chile strike.
newsitem.headline: Asian copper higher, traders focus on Chile strike.

text.p: Asian trading was thin on Thursday due to Japan's "Golden Week" holiday, but traders said they would keep a close eye on strikes by Chilean copper mine workers to see what effect they would have on the metal price.
Three-month copper was quoted at $2,390/2,394 per tonne at 0700 GMT, against Wednesday's LME close of $2,379.
Chile, a major copper producer, has been hit by a rash of strikes at two of its copper mines, the giant Escondida and the Quebrada Blanca.
A small group of workers at the 800,000-tonne-a-year Escondida copper, owned by Broken Hill Proprietary and RTZ-CRA, have been on strike for a week and a half.
Workers at the 75,000-tonne-a-year Quebrada Blanca mine also went on strike on Wednesday after talks on wage negotiations broke down.

Japanese traders expect LME copper prices to remain volatile, fluctuating between $2,350 and $2,450 a tonne until late next week. The local physical market will remain quiet this week in Japan due to the Golden Week holiday, traders said. -- Tokyo Commodities Desk (+81-3-3432-7391)
